newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may slash telecoms investment - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may slash telecoms investment - paper.

text.p: Brazil may cut 1997 investment in the state-run telecommuncations sector to seven billion reais from an originally budgeted 8.5 billion reais to reduce the federal budget deficit, Folha de Sao Paulo said Sunday.

The newspaper said federally owned telecommunications giant Telebras had informed its 28 subsidiaries that the State Business Coordination and Control Council (CCE) had decided on the cuts as part of an overall effort to rein in public spending.
But the paper quoted Telebras President Fernando Xavier Ferreira as saying the cuts were not certain yet.
"We have some room to maneuver and we're trying to reduce the impact of the cuts on investments," Ferreira said.
The paper listed the following impacts on leading Telebras subsidiaries under the proposed cuts:
* Investments in Telesp, which serves the state of Sao Paulo, would fall to 1.86 billion reais from 2.3 billion reais.
* Investments in Telerj, which serves the state of Rio de Janeiro, would fall to 950 million reais from 1.1 billion.
* Investments in Telebahia, which serves the state of Bahia, would fall to 278 million reais from 310 million reais.
